channel.title: Personal AI Agents (Update Bot)
channel.description: Latest features and updates for personal AI agents: Grok Bot, Hermes Agent, Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots.

item.title: Hermes Agent named to TIME's Best Inventions of 2026
item.description:
TIME put Nous Research's open-source Hermes Agent on its Best Inventions of 2026 list, published Oct 15, calling it "an infinitely modifiable agent that grows with you."

The write-up highlights that Hermes runs on any local or cloud model, lets users restyle its interface and write their own skills, and can run terminal commands, edit files and schedule recurring work. Nous Research thanked TIME in an X post with a screenshot of the listing (about 1,200 likes).

Coverage: RuntimeWire.

item.title: Hermes Agent gets an official Reverse Engineer Anything plugin
item.description:
Hermes Agent now has an official plugin for Reverse Engineer Anything (REA), an open-source toolkit for having agents reverse engineer apps, from their behavior down to native binaries.

One command, hermes plugins install rea, sets up the MCP config plus a dedicated skill for the agent, according to @tonbistudio's walkthrough video. Nous co-founder Teknium promoted the guide and @NousResearch reposted it.

item.title: OpenAI dots get GPT-Live-1.1 voices with better accents and new languages
item.description:
OpenAI announced on Oct 15 that its new voice model GPT-Live-1.1 is coming to Voice in ChatGPT, Codex and dots, its always-on agents. The update brings new voices, better accents and less repetitive "checking..." filler while it searches.

  • New voices in French, German, Hindi, Mexican Spanish, Korean and Japanese.
  • Rolling out to all users now; API access is coming soon.

Details: GPT-Live-1.1 system card. Dots pricing and post-launch usage terms are still unpublished.

item.title: Schwab blocks Meta's Muse and other AI agents from moving client money
item.description:
Charles Schwab is blocking outside AI agents, including Meta's Muse, when they try to move client money, CEO Rick Wurster told Bloomberg Television on Friday, The Next Web reports. He said the concern is clients handing their passwords to an agent that then acts for them, and that big agents get stopped "in the tens and twenties" each week.

Schwab plans to offer controlled MCP servers so outside AI tools can check balances and do research, but not move money, and wants clients to use its own assistant, Charley. JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon took a similar stance on outside agents earlier this week.

item.title: Hermes Agent v0.22.2: corrective release after bad v0.22.1 build
item.description:
Nous Research shipped Hermes Agent v0.22.2 today. Official notes say v0.22.1 was built from the wrong commit: it shipped unreleased gateway work, and the Microsoft Store app could stick on "Connecting." 0.22.2 is the release 0.22.1 was meant to be.

Highlights: the gateway starts after a reboot again (supervised installs could refuse to start when Linux handed an early PID to an unrelated process), and long local-model turns survive better on laptops (streaming progress, stall timers skip sleep time, recovered local servers get another try). Known issue: sessions that ran under the 0.22.1 gateway can't be deleted in 0.22.2.

Primary source: GitHub release v0.22.2. Prior threshold release: v0.22.0.

item.title: Grok Bot computers degradation resolved (incident 6y0yq43mvwg2)
item.description:
Cursor marked the Oct 14 Grok Bot service degradation as Resolved at 2:04pm PT (21:04 UTC). The incident (status.cursor.com id 6y0yq43mvwg2) had blocked some users from reaching their Bot computers since 8:46am PT; it moved from Investigating to Identified at 1:08pm PT, then to Resolved.

Status page now shows All Systems Operational, including Grok Bot. If a computer still looks stuck, try Recover / Update Bot's Computer or reopen the app. Earlier item: degradation note (guid updatebot-agents-2026-10-14-grok-bot-computers-degradation).

item.title: Grok Bot degradation: some users can't reach their computers (investigating since 8:46am PT)
item.description:
Since 8:46am PT (15:46 UTC) on Oct 14, the Cursor status page has listed Grok Bot as Degraded Performance, saying some users can't reach their computers. As of about 11am PT the incident was still Investigating, with no fix posted. All other Cursor components were operational.

This follows yesterday's resolved incident in which many webhook, Slack, git, email and Linear routines didn't run between 10:52am and 1:29pm PT; those events won't be retried automatically. The latest Grok Bot release is still v0.70.2.

item.title: OpenAI Dots Help adds troubleshooting answers; pricing unchanged, post-launch usage terms still unpublished
item.description:
OpenAI updated Getting started with your dot with troubleshooting answers. Each task has its own conversation, so give corrections in the affected task. Changing the selected computer doesn't move existing tasks. Read access to an app doesn't include write access. The cloud browser has its own sign-ins, and only the desktop app can grant local access.

Pricing is unchanged: the first dot is included at no extra cost with Pro 100/200/500 ($100/$200/$500 a month) or Business Premium. Chatting with a dot doesn't count toward limits, but Work and Codex tasks it starts do. The "extended limits for the first month" window and its follow-on terms are still unpublished and are expected around Oct 29 (gptdot.net tracker). GPT-5.5 retires from ChatGPT, Work and Codex today, but dots run on GPT-6 Astra.

item.title: Meta's Muse agent to move to Muse Wonder, subscribers first
item.description:
Meta says its new Muse Wonder model "will soon power experiences in Muse," rolling out to subscribers first. It will also handle artifact generation and other tasks that need more intelligence (Meta).

The models add Active Memory, which carries context across conversations, and Active Focus, which keeps long tasks going and checks in before important actions. Muse has run on Muse Spark since its Sept. 8 U.S. launch (SiliconANGLE). For developers, Muse Wonder is on the Meta Model API at $4/$20 per million tokens (Meta dev blog).

item.title: Breaking: Hermes Agent v0.22.0 — The Threshold Release
item.description:
Nous Research shipped Hermes Agent v0.22.0 (The Threshold Release), the largest Hermes window yet — about 2.5× the v0.21.0 cycle, rolling up v0.21.1–v0.21.7.

Highlights include guided first-launch setup on a free trial model, Connectors so Hermes can act in hosted apps like Linear and Notion without needing a Nous account to start, one-click local models via llama.cpp, tested SemVer stable release channels, signed desktop packages (including the Microsoft Store), and a 600-plugin catalog. Also in the wave: Claude 5.5 / GPT-6 model support, password-manager browser sign-in, and Bot Screen takeover.

Primary source: GitHub release v0.22.0.
